correctness.rationale: Every nonidentity kernel element has order p. For j=1,…,q-1, fixed-point-freeness makes c^j-1 invertible, while (1+c^j+…+c^{(q-1)j})(c^j-1)=0, so every vc^j has order exactly q. This gives the two ψ formulas. Frobenius orbits on V\{0} give q|(p^r-1); hence D=p^{r+1}-p+1 is congruent to one modulo p and q. The gcd therefore reduces to gcd(D,q-1), which is strictly smaller than D because q-1<p^r<D. An independent arithmetic sweep checked the gcd identity on 53 feasible small (p,r,q) triples; the proof is universal.

final_claim: If G=C_p^r⋊C_q is a Frobenius group with distinct primes p,q, rank r≥2 and prime complement, then ψ(C_p^r)=p^{r+1}-p+1, ψ(G)=p^{r+1}-p+1+p^r q(q-1), and gcd(ψ(C_p^r),ψ(G))=gcd(p^{r+1}-p+1,q-1)<ψ(C_p^r); hence G is not ψ-divisible.
scientific_limitations: An equivalent obstruction could occur in unindexed Frobenius-group sum-of-element-orders literature without the term ψ-divisible.
The complement is required to have prime order and the kernel to be elementary abelian.
